chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ibrahim ibn Hashim from Abd al-Rahman ibn Hammam from Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Hamid from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him)
Regarding a woman who said to a man, 'The private part of my slave girl is lawful for you,' so he had intercourse with her and she bore a child, he said: 'The child is valued for him at its price.'

key_terms.فَرْجُ: Private part (often used metonymically for sexual access or marriageability)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling for a child born from a slave girl when her owner declares her private part lawful to a man?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the phrase 'frj' (private part) is interpreted as a metaphor for the slave girl herself, establishing the validity of the sexual union. The ruling that the child is 'valued' (yuqammam) implies that the father must pay the mother's owner the market value of the child, a mechanism known as 'tadhim' or compensation, which secures the child's status and lineage while settling the financial rights of the owner.
